titulo: Reported Speech, Backshift and Hedged Attribution
descripcion: At C2 the three layers of distance are calibrated to legal and journalistic risk: the choice between allegedly and reportedly can carry defamation implications, and the decision to backshift or not can itself signal whether a claim is still considered true. This is precision as professional responsibility, not just style.

cuadroReferencia.titulo: Distance as legal and editorial signal
filas: implies wrongdoing not yet proven — carries legal weight
distances from a claim without implying guilt
the claim is treated as still current and possibly true
distances the claim in time, sometimes implying doubt now

ejemplos.texto: The company allegedly falsified the safety records.
Officials reportedly discussed the matter last week.
He maintains that he is innocent.

notas: Allegedly is the standard word for an accusation not yet proven in court — using it carelessly, or omitting it where wrongdoing is implied, carries real editorial and legal risk.
Choosing not to backshift (he says he is, not he said he was) signals that the reporter still considers the claim potentially current, not just historical.
This calibration is what separates careful journalism and legal writing from a merely grammatically correct report.

es.en: Spanish uses presuntamente much like allegedly, so the legal concept is familiar. The English choice between keeping or shifting the tense as a deliberate editorial signal has no such explicit equivalent in Spanish, where backshift is more automatic and carries less intention.
es.es: El español usa «presuntamente» de forma muy parecida a «allegedly», por lo que el concepto jurídico es familiar. La elección inglesa entre mantener o desplazar el tiempo verbal como señal editorial deliberada no tiene un equivalente tan explícito en español, donde el backshift es más automático y transmite menos intención.

de.en: German marks reported speech with the Konjunktiv I, which does not change with the time of reporting, so the idea that keeping or shifting the tense can itself carry an editorial signal is new. Angeblich sounds more sceptical than allegedly; the closer legal match is mutmasslich (the alleged offender – der mutmassliche Täter).
de.de: Deutsch markiert indirekte Rede mit Konjunktiv I, der sich mit dem Zeitpunkt des Berichtens nicht verändert. Die Idee, dass Beibehalten oder Verschieben der Zeitform selbst ein redaktionelles Signal tragen kann, ist daher neu. «Angeblich» klingt skeptischer als «allegedly»; die nähere juristische Entsprechung ist «mutmaßlich» («the alleged offender» – «der mutmaßliche Täter»).

it.en: Italian journalism marks unconfirmed claims with the condizionale (il ministro avrebbe detto), which leads to the calque the minister would have said instead of reportedly said or is said to have said. Presunto corresponds well to alleged.
it.it: Il giornalismo italiano segnala affermazioni non confermate con il condizionale («il ministro avrebbe detto»), il che porta al calco «the minister would have said» invece di «reportedly said» o «is said to have said». «Presunto» corrisponde bene a «alleged».

fr.en: The French conditionnel journalistique (le ministre aurait déclaré) leads to the calque the minister would have declared. Présumé corresponds to alleged, while prétendument is more sceptical and closer to supposedly, so French speakers need to keep these two apart in English.
fr.fr: Le conditionnel journalistique français («le ministre aurait déclaré») conduit au calque «the minister would have declared». «Présumé» correspond à «alleged», tandis que «prétendument» est plus sceptique et se rapproche de «supposedly» ; il faut donc bien distinguer les deux en anglais.

pt.en: European Portuguese press uses alegadamente very much like allegedly, so the legal concept is familiar. Unconfirmed claims are also marked with the future perfect (o ministro terá dito), which leads to the calque the minister will have said instead of reportedly said.
pt.pt: A imprensa portuguesa europeia usa «alegadamente» de modo muito parecido com «allegedly», então o conceito jurídico é familiar. Afirmações não confirmadas também podem ser marcadas com o futuro perfeito («o ministro terá dito»), o que pode levar ao calque «the minister will have said» em vez de «reportedly said».

errores: Omitting allegedly where an accusation of wrongdoing is being reported as fact.
Backshifting automatically without considering whether the claim should read as still current.
Confusing allegedly and reportedly, which carry different legal and editorial weight.

redemittel.funcion: no backshift, claim treated as current

traducciones.fr: Il a affirmé qu’il avait été…

redemittel.expresion: We have not independently verified this.
redemittel.funcion: states the limit of the reporting

traducciones.es: No hemos verificado esto de forma independiente.
traducciones.de: Wir haben das nicht unabhängig überprüft.
traducciones.fr: Nous n'avons pas vérifié cela de façon indépendante.
traducciones.it: Non l'abbiamo verificato in modo indipendente.
traducciones.pt: Não verificámos isto de forma independente.

redemittel.funcion: puts two reported versions in conflict

traducciones.es: Ambas versiones no pueden ser ciertas.
traducciones.fr: Les deux versions ne peuvent pas être vraies.
traducciones.it: Entrambe le versioni non possono essere vere.
traducciones.pt: As duas versões não podem ser verdadeiras.

redemittel.expresion: That wording came from the press release.

traducciones.de: Diese Formulierung stammt aus der Pressemitteilung.

redemittel.expresion: Here I'm speaking in my own voice.
redemittel.funcion: marks the exit from reported speech

traducciones.es: Acá hablo con mi propia voz.
traducciones.de: Hier spreche ich mit eigener Stimme.
traducciones.fr: Ici, je parle en mon nom.
traducciones.it: Qui parlo con la mia voce.
traducciones.pt: Aqui falo com a minha própria voz.

redemittel.funcion: separates the verified from the reported

traducciones.de: Belegt ist nur der zeitliche Ablauf.

autochequeo: Is allegedly used precisely where wrongdoing is implied but unproven?
Is the backshift decision deliberate, signalling whether the claim is still current?
Are allegedly and reportedly correctly distinguished?
Would this wording survive legal or editorial scrutiny in a professional publication?
Would an editor or lawyer flag anything here as risky?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the legal and editorial precision of hedged attribution. Check allegedly versus reportedly and whether the backshift decision is deliberate. Do not rewrite the text.

de: *mutmasslich* rendered as *presumably* in a report of wrongdoing, instead of *alleged* or *suspected*.
it: «*il presunto colpevole*» rendered as *the presumed culprit* instead of *the alleged culprit*.
fr: *l'auteur présumé* rendered as *the presumed perpetrator* instead of *the alleged perpetrator*.
pt: *o presumível autor* rendered as *the presumable perpetrator* instead of *the alleged perpetrator*.
